slides.title: Systems
slides.raw:
Systems
Endpoint Protection Platforms (EPP)
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.
defs: Security Information and Event Management: centralizes and correlates logs/events for alerting, search, and investigation.

course.learn: This section focuses on **Systems** within **Monitoring computing resources**. System monitoring focuses on endpoints and hosts. Endpoint Protection Platforms (EPP) detect or prevent malicious endpoint activity, while SIEM platforms collect and correlate events from many systems.
course.why: Host-level visibility shows processes, files, authentication, and local behavior that network monitoring may not see.
course.example: An EPP quarantines a malicious executable and forwards the event to the SIEM for correlation with identity and firewall logs.
course.exam: EPP = endpoint protection. SIEM = centralized event/log correlation.

breakdown.explanation: Within Systems, this is a specific factor you should be able to recognize and explain. Connect it to the purpose of Monitoring computing resources rather than memorizing the phrase by itself.
This contributes to reducing risk in the broader Monitoring computing resources design and should be evaluated as part of defense in depth.

slides.title: Application
slides.raw:
Application
Application Performance
Monitoring (APM)
Web Application Firewalls
(WAF)
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.
defs: Web Application Firewall: filters HTTP/HTTPS traffic to protect web applications.

course.learn: This section focuses on **Application** within **Monitoring computing resources**. Application monitoring measures application behavior, performance, errors, and security events. APM focuses on health/performance, while a WAF inspects and protects web requests.
course.why: Application-layer problems may not be visible from host or network metrics alone.
course.example: APM shows a sudden increase in database latency while the WAF reports blocked injection attempts against the same application.
course.exam: APM = performance/health; WAF = web application security filtering.

breakdown.explanation: Application monitoring measures application behavior, performance, errors, and security events. APM focuses on health/performance, while a WAF inspects and protects web requests.
Security monitoring continuously observes systems, networks, applications, and logs for suspicious activity, failures, policy violations, and indicators of compromise.
Filter network traffic according to security rules, usually by source, destination, protocol, port, application, or context.
A Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic with awareness of web requests and application-layer attacks.

defs.definition: Web Application Firewall: filters HTTP/HTTPS traffic to protect web applications.

slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.
defs: Computing resources delivered on demand from a provider rather than entirely owned and operated locally.
Cloud Security Posture Management: tools/processes that identify risky cloud configuration and compliance issues.

course.learn: This section focuses on **Infrastructure** within **Monitoring computing resources**. Infrastructure monitoring observes networks, cloud configuration, appliances, links, and supporting resources. NSM analyzes network behavior, while CSPM evaluates cloud security posture and misconfiguration.
course.why: Infrastructure telemetry helps detect both attacks and unsafe configuration drift.
course.example: CSPM flags a public storage bucket while NSM detects unusual outbound traffic from a server subnet.
course.exam: NSM = network activity. CSPM = cloud configuration/posture.
